```{r}

# ============================================================
# FOUR-MODEL ANALYSIS
# ORGANIZATIONS WITH AT LEAST 50 ATTACKS
#
# Revised model numbering:
# Model 0 = Null model
# Model 1 = Ideology + year fixed effects
# Model 2 = Former Model 4, now the main model
# Model 3 = Former Model 5, tactical robustness
# ============================================================


# ============================================================
# 0. INSTALL AND LOAD PACKAGES
# ============================================================

required_packages <- c(
  "readxl",
  "dplyr",
  "tidyr",
  "stringr",
  "lme4",
  "broom.mixed",
  "emmeans",
  "ggplot2",
  "readr"
)

packages_to_install <- required_packages[
  !required_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())
]

if (length(packages_to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(packages_to_install)
}

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(lme4)
library(broom.mixed)
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)


# ============================================================
# 1. FILE LOCATION
# ============================================================

file_path <- paste0(
  "D:/PhD in Political Science-UTD/Field Paper/Data/",
  "GTD-India_Avinash_with_Districts_and_OCI_",
  "MatchedData_with_Controls_Final 2.xlsx"

      "\n\nCurrent working directory:\n",
      getwd(),
      "\n\nChange file_path to the actual location of the Excel file."
    )

}

# 2. READ BOTH WORKSHEETS

cat("Sheet 2 rows:", nrow(sheet2), "\n")

# ============================================================
# 4. PREPARE SHEET 2 ORGANIZATION REFERENCE
# ============================================================

focal_categories <- c(
  "Maoist",
  "Islamist",
  "Separatist/Ethnonationalist"
)

organization_reference <- sheet2 %>%
  transmute(
    organization = str_squish(as.character(Organization)),
    total_count = as.numeric(Total_Count),
    ideology_sheet2 = str_squish(
      as.character(Ideological_Category)
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    ideology_sheet2 %in% focal_categories,
    total_count >= 50
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    organization,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    ideology_sheet2,
    desc(total_count)
  )

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("ORGANIZATIONS MEETING THE 50-ATTACK THRESHOLD\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(
  organization_reference,

)

eligible_summary <- organization_reference %>%

  summarise(
    eligible_organizations = n_distinct(organization),

  )

# ============================================================
# 5. PREPARE SHEET 1
# ============================================================

incident_data <- sheet1 %>%
  mutate(
    organization = str_squish(as.character(gname)),
    
    target_category = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(as.character(`Target Category`))
    ),
    
    ideology_code = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(as.character(ideology_code))
    ),
    
    year_numeric = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(as.character(iyear))
    ),
    
    OCI = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(OCI)
    ),
    
    lagged_district_terrorism_intensity =
      suppressWarnings(
        as.numeric(lagged_district_terrorism_intensity)
      ),
    
    attacktype1 = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(as.character(attacktype1))
    ),
    
    weaptype1 = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(as.character(weaptype1))
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 6. CREATE LOGGED DISTRICT TERRORISM INTENSITY
# ============================================================

# Sheet 1 contains the unlogged variable.
# log1p(x) calculates ln(1 + x).

incident_data <- incident_data %>%
  mutate(
    ln_lagged_district_terrorism_intensity =
      log1p(lagged_district_terrorism_intensity)
  )


# ============================================================
# 7. FILTER SHEET 1 USING ELIGIBLE ORGANIZATIONS FROM SHEET 2
# ============================================================

threshold_sample <- incident_data %>%
  inner_join(
    organization_reference,
    by = "organization"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    ideology_code %in% c(1, 2, 3)
  )

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

# ============================================================
# 9. CREATE A COMMON ANALYTICAL SAMPLE
# ============================================================

# All four models use the same observations.
# Including Model 3 variables here ensures that differences between
# models are not caused by changes in the sample.

required_model_variables <- c(
  "target_category",
  "organization",
  "year_numeric",
  "ideology_code",
  "OCI",
  "conflict_region",
  "ln_lagged_district_terrorism_intensity",
  "attacktype1",
  "weaptype1"
)

analysis <- threshold_sample %>%
  filter(
    if_all(
      all_of(required_model_variables),
      ~ !is.na(.x)
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    target_category %in% c(0, 1)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ideology = factor(
      ideology_code,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "Maoist",
        "Separatist/Ethnonationalist",
        "Islamist"
      )
    ),
    
    # Maoist is the reference ideology.
    ideology = relevel(
      ideology,
      ref = "Maoist"
    ),
    
    conflict_region = factor(
      str_squish(as.character(conflict_region))
    ),
    
    # Rest of India is the reference conflict region.
    conflict_region = relevel(
      conflict_region,
      ref = "Rest of India"
    ),
    
    # Year is categorical, creating year fixed effects.
    year = factor(year_numeric),
    
    # Organization is the random-intercept grouping variable.
    organization = factor(organization),
    
    # Tactical controls are categorical.
    attack_type = factor(attacktype1),
    weapon_type = factor(weaptype1)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

# ============================================================
# 12. MODEL CONTROL SETTINGS
# ============================================================

model_control <- glmerControl(
  optimizer = "bobyqa",
  optCtrl = list(
    maxfun = 200000
  ),
  calc.derivs = TRUE
)


# ============================================================
# MODEL 0
# NULL MIXED-EFFECTS LOGISTIC REGRESSION
# ============================================================

model0 <- glmer(
  target_category ~
    1 +
    (1 | organization),
  
  data = analysis,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  control = model_control,
  nAGQ = 1
)


# ============================================================
# MODEL 1
# IDEOLOGY + YEAR FIXED EFFECTS
# ============================================================

model1 <- glmer(
  target_category ~
    ideology +
    year +
    (1 | organization),
  
  data = analysis,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  control = model_control,
  nAGQ = 1
)


# ============================================================
# MODEL 2
# MAIN MODEL
# FORMER MODEL 4 IN THE PYTHON NOTEBOOK
# ============================================================

model2 <- glmer(
  target_category ~
    ideology * OCI +
    conflict_region +
    ln_lagged_district_terrorism_intensity +
    year +
    (1 | organization),
  
  data = analysis,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  control = model_control,
  nAGQ = 1
)


# ============================================================
# MODEL 3
# TACTICAL ROBUSTNESS MODEL
# FORMER MODEL 5 IN THE PYTHON NOTEBOOK
# ============================================================

model3 <- glmer(
  target_category ~
    ideology * OCI +
    conflict_region +
    ln_lagged_district_terrorism_intensity +
    attack_type +
    weapon_type +
    year +
    (1 | organization),
  
  data = analysis,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  control = model_control,
  nAGQ = 1
)

# ============================================================
# 14. FIXED-EFFECT TABLE FUNCTION
# ============================================================

fixed_effect_table <- function(model, model_name) {
  
  broom.mixed::tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE,
    conf.method = "Wald",
    exponentiate = FALSE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Model = model_name,
      odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
      OR_conf_low = exp(conf.low),
      OR_conf_high = exp(conf.high)
    ) %>%
    select(
      Model,
      term,
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic,
      p.value,
      conf.low,
      conf.high,
      odds_ratio,
      OR_conf_low,
      OR_conf_high
    )
}

table_model0 <- fixed_effect_table(
  model0,
  "Model 0"
)

table_model1 <- fixed_effect_table(
  model1,
  "Model 1"
)

table_model2 <- fixed_effect_table(
  model2,
  "Model 2: Main model"
)

table_model3 <- fixed_effect_table(
  model3,
  "Model 3: Tactical robustness"
)

all_fixed_effects <- bind_rows(
  table_model0,
  table_model1,
  table_model2,
  table_model3
)

cat("\nFixed-effect results:\n")
print(
  all_fixed_effects,
  n = Inf
)


# ============================================================
# 15. RANDOM-EFFECT AND ICC FUNCTION
# ============================================================

random_effect_diagnostics <- function(model, model_name) {
  
  variance_table <- as.data.frame(
    VarCorr(model)
  )
  
  organization_variance <- variance_table %>%
    filter(
      grp == "organization",
      var1 == "(Intercept)"
    ) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    pull(vcov)
  
  organization_sd <- sqrt(
    organization_variance
  )
  
  logistic_level1_variance <- pi^2 / 3
  
  ICC <- organization_variance /
    (
      organization_variance +
        logistic_level1_variance
    )
  
  tibble(
    Model = model_name,
    organization_variance =
      organization_variance,
    organization_SD =
      organization_sd,
    ICC = ICC,
    ICC_percentage = 100 * ICC
  )
}

random_effects_table <- bind_rows(
  random_effect_diagnostics(
    model0,
    "Model 0"
  ),
  
  random_effect_diagnostics(
    model1,
    "Model 1"
  ),
  
  random_effect_diagnostics(
    model2,
    "Model 2: Main model"
  ),
  
  random_effect_diagnostics(
    model3,
    "Model 3: Tactical robustness"
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("RANDOM EFFECTS AND ICC\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(random_effects_table)

# ============================================================
# 17. CONVERGENCE CHECK
# ============================================================

convergence_status <- function(model, model_name) {
  
  messages <- model@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages
  
  tibble(
    Model = model_name,
    convergence_warning = if (
      is.null(messages)
    ) {
      "None"
    } else {
      paste(messages, collapse = " | ")
    },
    singular_fit = isSingular(
      model,
      tol = 1e-4
    )
  )
}

convergence_table <- bind_rows(
  convergence_status(model0, "Model 0"),
  convergence_status(model1, "Model 1"),
  convergence_status(
    model2,
    "Model 2: Main model"
  ),
  convergence_status(
    model3,
    "Model 3: Tactical robustness"
  )
)

cat("\nConvergence diagnostics:\n")
print(convergence_table)

  summary(
    model3_pairwise_slopes,
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 21. IDEOLOGY × CONFLICT-REGION OVERLAP
# ============================================================

overlap_counts <- table(
  analysis$ideology,
  analysis$conflict_region
)

overlap_row_percentages <- prop.table(
  overlap_counts,
  margin = 1
) * 100

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("IDEOLOGY × CONFLICT-REGION COUNTS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(overlap_counts)

cat("\nRow percentages:\n")
print(
  round(
    overlap_row_percentages,
    2
  )
)

chi_square_result <- suppressWarnings(
  chisq.test(overlap_counts)
)

cramers_v <- sqrt(
  as.numeric(chi_square_result$statistic) /
    (
      sum(overlap_counts) *
        min(
          nrow(overlap_counts) - 1,
          ncol(overlap_counts) - 1
        )
    )
)

cat(
  "\nCramer's V:",
  round(cramers_v, 4),
  "\n"
)

# ============================================================
# 22. MODEL 2 PREDICTED PROBABILITIES
# MEMORY-EFFICIENT VERSION
# ============================================================

OCI_grid <- seq(
  from = as.numeric(
    quantile(
      analysis$OCI,
      0.05,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ),
  to = as.numeric(
    quantile(
      analysis$OCI,
      0.95,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ),
  length.out = 30
)

# Year and conflict region do not interact with ideology or OCI.
# Treating them as nuisance factors averages over their observed
# distributions without creating every possible combination.

model2_predictions <- emmeans(
  model2,
  specs = ~ ideology | OCI,
  at = list(
    OCI = OCI_grid
  ),
  nuisance = c(
    "year",
    "conflict_region"
  ),
  wt.nuis = "proportional",
  type = "response"
)

model2_prediction_data <- as.data.frame(
  summary(
    model2_predictions,
    type = "response"
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("MODEL 2 PREDICTED PROBABILITIES\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(model2_prediction_data)


# ============================================================
# 23. MODEL 2 PREDICTED-PROBABILITY GRAPH
# ============================================================

# Identify the response-probability column produced by emmeans.
# It is normally called "prob".

probability_column <- intersect(
  c("prob", "response", "emmean"),
  names(model2_prediction_data)
)[1]

if (is.na(probability_column)) {
  stop(
    "Could not identify the predicted-probability column. ",
    "Run names(model2_prediction_data) to inspect the output."
  )
}

# Identify the confidence-interval columns.
lower_column <- intersect(
  c("asymp.LCL", "lower.CL"),
  names(model2_prediction_data)
)[1]

upper_column <- intersect(
  c("asymp.UCL", "upper.CL"),
  names(model2_prediction_data)
)[1]

if (
  is.na(lower_column) ||
  is.na(upper_column)
) {
  stop(
    "Could not identify the confidence-interval columns. ",
    "Run names(model2_prediction_data) to inspect the output."
  )
}

plot_data <- model2_prediction_data %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_probability =
      .data[[probability_column]],
    confidence_lower =
      .data[[lower_column]],
    confidence_upper =
      .data[[upper_column]]
  )

prediction_graph <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = OCI,
    y = predicted_probability,
    color = ideology,
    fill = ideology
  )
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = confidence_lower,
      ymax = confidence_upper
    ),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Operational Capacity Index (OCI)",
    y = "Predicted probability of hard-target selection",
    color = "Ideology",
    fill = "Ideology"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 12
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(prediction_graph)



# ============================================================
# 24. SAVE RESULTS
# ============================================================

  dirname(file_path),

if (!dir.exists(output_directory)) {
```
